description:
Characterize the optical resolution of the microscope system by measuring the Point Spread Function (PSF).

1. Open the bead image at `~/Fiji_Data/raw/psf_beads/bead_field.tif`.
2. Set the spatial calibration using `Analyze > Set Scale`. The pixel size is **0.1625 µm/pixel** (or 6.154 pixels/µm).
3. Measure the **Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM)** of at least **5 isolated bead-like features**.
   - Use the Line tool to draw a line across the center of a bead.
   - Use `Analyze > Plot Profile` (Ctrl+K) to generate the intensity profile.
   - Measure the width of the peak at half of its maximum intensity (FWHM).
4. Save your measurements to `~/Fiji_Data/results/psf/fwhm_measurements.csv` with columns: `bead_id`, `fwhm_pixels`, `fwhm_um`, `peak_intensity`.
5. Save one representative line profile plot as an image to `~/Fiji_Data/results/psf/line_profile.png`.
6. Save a summary report to `~/Fiji_Data/results/psf/resolution_report.txt` stating the **mean FWHM in µm** (this is the system's lateral resolution).

Goal: Accurately estimate the resolution. The FWHM should be consistent across beads.
